knowledge_point.title: Sketching a Line Using Two Points

question.:question/problem: Which of the following graphs shows the line $y=x?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We need to find two distinct points that lie on our line. Any two points will do!

- For the first point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=0.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =x \\  & =(0) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the first point is $(0,0).$

- For the second point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=-1.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =x \\  & =(-1) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second point is $(-1,-1).$

Finally, we plot those two points on the $xy$-plane and draw a line through them. This is the graph of $y=x.$ 

![](images/0e/0ea48502e9b158b482c27ff585183cbbf49e148d47ba6cbc642df9ec2e060425.png)

Finally, we plot those two points on the $xy$-plane and draw a line through them. This is the graph of $y=-3x.$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following graphs shows the line $y=- \frac{2}{3}x-3?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We need to find two distinct points that lie on our line. Any two points will do!

- For the first point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=0.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =- \frac{2}{3}x-3 \\  & =- \frac{2}{3}(0)-3 \\  & =0-3 \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the first point is $(0,-3).$

- For the second point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=-3.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =- \frac{2}{3}x-3 \\  & =- \frac{2}{3}(-3)-3 \\  & =2-3 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second point is $(-3,-1).$

Finally, we plot those two points on the $xy$-plane and draw a line through them. This is the graph of $y=- \frac{2}{3}x-3.$

![](images/b2/b20b2c45c0ae741b6e2ecbb5414acca77f97ab45da286a883ec8c1604d387f00.png)

\begin{aligned}y & =- \frac{3}{2}x+2 \\  & =- \frac{3}{2}(0)+2 \\  & =0+2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem: Which of the following graphs shows the line $y=- \frac{4}{3}x+\frac{7}{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We need to find two distinct points that lie on our line. Any two points will do!

- For the first point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=0.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =- \frac{4}{3}x+\frac{7}{2} \\  & =- \frac{4}{3}(0)+\frac{7}{2} \\  & =0+\frac{7}{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the first point is $(0,\frac{7}{2}).$

- For the second point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=-3.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =- \frac{4}{3}x+\frac{7}{2} \\  & =- \frac{4}{3}(-3)+\frac{7}{2} \\  & =4+\frac{7}{2} \\  & =\frac{15}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second point is $(-3,\frac{15}{2}).$

Finally, we plot those two points on the $xy$-plane and draw a line through them. This is the graph of $y=- \frac{4}{3}x+\frac{7}{2}.$
